title: Smooth projective completions of curve normalizations after inseparable extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a separated finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with $\dim X\leq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There are a finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], a finite set $I$, finite separable extensions $k_i/k'$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and a diagram over $k'$ $$\coprod_{i\in I}Y_i\xrightarrow{\nu}X_{k'},\qquad Y_i\xrightarrow{j_i}\overline Y_i\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(k_i).$$ Here $X_{k'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $\nu$ is the normalization: explicitly the disjoint union of the normalizations of the reduced irreducible components of $(X_{k'})_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-normalization] [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Each $j_i$ is an open immersion with dense nonempty image [def-weil-open-immersion]. Each $\overline Y_i$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], projective [def-kun-projective], and geometrically irreducible over $k_i$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], with dimension at most one. All the schemes displayed are of finite presentation over $k'$. The set $I$ is empty precisely when $X$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0GK5, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion-after-insep, assertions (1)-(5); normalization interpreted componentwise as in its normalization section

proof.text: Take a dense projective completion D of X directly, without first reducing X. The completion theorem applies to nonreduced and empty schemes. Regard D as a scheme over k via its displayed structure map.

source.place: Tag 0GK5, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion-after-insep, assertions (1)-(5); normalization interpreted componentwise as in its normalization section

proof.text: Apply finite purely inseparable geometric normalization to D. It supplies a finite family of integral closed components Z_i of D_K, without repetitions and covering its irreducible components, and geometrically normal stalks on the coproduct of their normalizations. Projectivity survives base change. The purely inseparable projection is a homeomorphism, so dim(D_K) <= 1.

source.place: Tag 0GK5, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion-after-insep, assertions (1)-(5); normalization interpreted componentwise as in its normalization section

proof.text: Each B_i = Z_i.normalization is finite over Z_i and hence over D_K. Finite over projective over the affine field base is projective. Normalization preserves dimension, and the closed component has dimension at most that of D_K. For each field extension, the map from the base change of B_i into the base change of the normalization coproduct is an open immersion. Its stalk isomorphisms transfer the supplied normal-domain stalks to B_i. Apply the geometric-normality dimension-one criterion to obtain smoothness of B_i.

source.place: Tag 0GK5, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion-after-insep, assertions (1)-(5); normalization interpreted componentwise as in its normalization section

proof.text: Put L_i = Gamma(B_i,O). Proper integrality makes this ring a field, finite over K. Smoothness gives geometric reducedness, so the global-sections separability theorem applies. For a finite algebraic extension its separably-generated criterion is ordinary Algebra.IsSeparable: apply it to the top intermediate field, note that an algebraically independent subset of an algebraic extension is empty, and transport separability from the bottom intermediate field. The canonical map q_i = B_i.toSpecGamma composes to the original structure map. Affine Stein factorization gives geometric connectedness, and finite separable base refinement gives smoothness and projectivity of q_i. After any field base change, smoothness makes the source regular and locally Noetherian; geometric connectedness makes it connected and nonempty, so it is integral and therefore irreducible. This proves geometric irreducibility without the separate etale-section argument.

source.place: Tag 0GK5, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion-after-insep, assertions (1)-(5); normalization interpreted componentwise as in its normalization section

proof.text: Base change the open immersion X -> D to a_K:X_K -> D_K. The homeomorphisms to X and D show that its image is the inverse image of the original dense open, hence dense. A dense open in a Noetherian space meets every irreducible component: delete the union of the other finitely many components to get a nonempty open whose closure is the chosen component. Define C_i = X_K times_{D_K} Z_i. Its map c_i to X_K is closed, and its map r_i to Z_i is open and nonempty, so C_i is integral. The range of c_i is a_K^{-1}(range z_i). Preimages along an open embedding of components meeting its image are components. Closure of their images recovers the original components, proving injectivity. Conversely the image of any irreducible component of X_K is contained in a component of D_K; maximality then gives equality with its preimage. Thus c_i enumerate all components of X_K.

source.place: Tag 0GK5, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion-after-insep, assertions (1)-(5); normalization interpreted componentwise as in its normalization section

proof.text: Set Y_i = C_i.normalization. Normalization restricts along the open immersion r_i. In Lean this is proved directly from Mathlib Scheme.Hom.normalizationPullback and its IsIso instance for smooth base change. Dominance sends the generic point of C_i to that of Z_i. The stalk isomorphism of r_i identifies their function-field spectra; the corresponding generic-point square is a pullback. Relative normalization is unchanged by an isomorphism of its source over its target (proved from normalizationDesc and hom_ext). Composing that identification with normalizationPullback gives the open immersion j_i:Y_i -> B_i and j_i ; Z_i.fromNormalization = C_i.fromNormalization ; r_i. Integral nonempty Y_i and B_i make its image dense. Take e_i to be the identity isomorphism and nu to be the coproduct of the normalization maps followed by c_i. Pullback commutativity and the structure equations give every displayed triangle.

source.place: Tag 0GK5, label lemma-dim-1-projective-completion-after-insep, assertions (1)-(5); normalization interpreted componentwise as in its normalization section

proof.text: Each Y_i has a finite normalization map over C_i, hence is separated and finite type over K. Each B_i and Spec L_i is likewise finite type, the latter by module finiteness. The finite coproduct of Y_i is compact by its canonical finite open cover and locally finite type by source locality; it is locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated. Over Spec K, local finite type implies local finite presentation. The same base-change instances supply the finite-presentation clauses for X_K. If n=0, the component covering forces X_K empty and the purely inseparable homeomorphism forces X empty. If X is empty, every C_i would map to the empty X_K, contradicting its nonemptiness; hence n=0. No separate empty-case construction is needed.
